record.what_it_does: Issue tracking and project management for software teams, with cycles, projects and roadmaps.
record.auth_notes: OAuth2 uses the authorization code flow, with PKCE supported and either the user or the app as actor (actor=app). Apps can also use client credentials, which issue app-actor tokens valid for 30 days with no refresh token; this has to be turned on per app. Authorization-code access tokens last 24h and refresh tokens last 30 days. Personal API keys are sent as a raw `Authorization: <API_KEY>` header. Keys can be limited to Read, Write, Admin, Create issues or Create comments, and to specific teams. OAuth tokens go in the Bearer header.
record.access_notes: The pricing page lists 'API and webhook access' as Included on the Free plan, with standard rate limits. Free is capped at 250 issues and 2 teams. Admins and permitted Members can create personal API keys, and admins can turn off key creation for Members. OAuth apps are created in workspace settings, and the docs describe no review step before other workspaces can authorize an app. Listing in Linear's Integration Directory is a separate, curated step: you submit a form and email integrations@linear.app. Distribution does not require it. Rate limits are 2,500 req/h per user for API keys and 5,000 req/h per user or app-user for OAuth apps. Creating or reading webhooks needs a workspace admin or the `admin` scope.
record.api_breadth_notes: A single GraphQL API at api.linear.app/graphql, the same one Linear uses internally. It covers issues, attachments, comments, labels, projects, project updates, cycles, documents, initiatives, customers and customer requests, teams and users. The schema supports introspection and there is a TypeScript SDK. I did not count operations, but the resources listed above put it well past 50.
record.mcp_notes: https://mcp.linear.app/mcp is read-write and https://mcp.linear.app/mcp/readonly is read-only. Transport is Streamable HTTP; the /sse endpoint is a deprecated fallback. The interactive flow uses OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration. The server also accepts `Authorization: Bearer <token>` with an OAuth token or an API key.
record.blocker_notes: There is no review gate for OAuth apps, and API and webhooks are included on the Free plan. The API is GraphQL only, so there is no OpenAPI spec. Linear has no dedicated sandbox, but a free workspace (250-issue cap) can serve as a test environment. Rate limits are 2,500 req/h for API keys and 5,000 req/h for OAuth apps, plus complexity-point limits.

evidence.quote: Each refresh token expires 30 days after issuance.
Client-credentials tokens use the `app` actor, are valid for 30 days, and do not include a refresh token.
To authenticate your requests, you need to pass the API key with header: `Authorization: <API_KEY>`
Admins and permitted Members can create personal API keys from Settings > Account > Security & Access.
It supports introspection so you can query the whole schema.
Only workspace admins, or OAuth applications with the `admin` scope, can create or read webhooks.
The interactive setup flow uses OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration.

changes.why: The personal API key is the only static credential. It is sent as a raw Authorization header, so it belongs under api_key. Listing bearer_token as well counted the same credential twice. OAuth access tokens are already covered by oauth2.
